predictions.selection_reason: Converts seconds to milliseconds for JavaScript Date constructor - critical for correct timestamp interpretation in client-side rendering
predictions.source_summary: item.time comes from Python backend's time.time() function via qute://history/data endpoint, stored as integer seconds in SQLite database (atime field)
predictions.sink_summary: JavaScript Date constructor used for session grouping and time display in browser history UI
predictions.guard_summary: No explicit validation - relies on backend ensuring valid timestamp format; backend uses int() conversion and SQLite integer storage
predictions.risk_pattern: Timestamp unit conversion from seconds to milliseconds for cross-language compatibility between Python backend and JavaScript frontend
predictions.context_summary: Converts backend timestamp (seconds) to JavaScript Date (milliseconds) for proper time display and session grouping in history page
unresolved_facts: Exact validation of timestamp bounds in backend
Potential for timestamp overflow if values are extremely large

retrieval_query.mechanism_summary: integer overflow in timestamp conversion, numeric range validation
retrieval_query.mechanism_keywords: integer overflow, arithmetic overflow, numeric conversion
